title: What PostgreSQL gives you out of the box
one_liner: PostgreSQL ships with rich data types, powerful SQL, procedural languages, full-text search, strong safety rules, data-integration tools and an extension system, all living in a few well-named source folders.
analogy: Think of PostgreSQL as a well-stocked workshop. The main room has the standard tools (types, SQL, constraints). The side rooms (src/pl, contrib) hold power tools you can switch on with one command (CREATE EXTENSION). Every tool has a label on the door, and that label is a source directory.
big_picture: Postgres is built so that almost everything is a catalog row: types, functions, operators, index methods, languages. That is why so many features can be added without changing the core.
The core engine lives in src/backend. Parser turns SQL into a tree, the rewriter and planner shape it, and the executor runs it. Most SQL features you use are a node type in one of those stages.
Built-in data types mostly live in src/backend/utils/adt (adt means abstract data type). One .c file per type family, for example jsonb.c, rangetypes.c, uuid.c, enum.c.
Procedural languages live in src/pl (plpgsql, plperl, plpython, tcl). Only plpgsql is installed in every new database by default.
Optional extras live in contrib. You turn one on with CREATE EXTENSION. On the 16.6 install I ran, 58 extensions were listed in pg_available_extensions.

Integration features are spread out: LISTEN/NOTIFY in src/backend/commands/async.c, COPY in src/backend/commands/copy*.c, logical decoding in src/backend/replication/logical, foreign data wrappers in src/backend/foreign plus contrib/postgres_fdw.

Version note: the repo is 20devel. I ran SQL on a scratch PostgreSQL 16.6 (the only server binary on this machine), so anything newer is checked in source only. MERGE ... RETURNING and merge_action() are 17+ (I saw the syntax error on 16.6, and merge_action is in primnodes.h). uuidv7 generation (generate_uuidv7 in uuid.c) is 18+. Virtual generated columns (ATTRIBUTE_GENERATED_VIRTUAL 'v' in pg_attribute.h) are 18+.

flow.detail: 1) Arrays: SELECT ARRAY[1,2,3] @> ARRAY[2]; (src/backend/utils/adt/arrayfuncs.c). 2) jsonb: SELECT '{"a":{"b":5}}'::jsonb #>> '{a,b}'; returns 5 (jsonb.c, jsonb_op.c, jsonb_gin.c). 3) Ranges: SELECT '[2024-01-01,2024-02-01)'::daterange * '[2024-01-15,2024-03-01)'::daterange; returns [2024-01-15,2024-02-01) (rangetypes.c, multirangetypes.c). 4) Enums: CREATE TYPE mood AS ENUM ('sad','ok','happy'); then 'ok'::mood < 'happy'::mood is true (enum.c, commands/typecmds.c). 5) Composite: CREATE TYPE pt AS (x int, y int); SELECT (row(1,2)::pt).y; (rowtypes.c). 6) uuid and text search types: SELECT gen_random_uuid(); (uuid.c) and to_tsvector/to_tsquery (tsvector.c, tsquery.c).

1) Recursive CTE: WITH RECURSIVE t(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM t WHERE n<5) SELECT sum(n) FROM t; gave 15 (nodeRecursiveunion.c, nodeCtescan.c, parser/parse_cte.c). 2) Window functions: SELECT x, sum(x) OVER (ORDER BY x) FROM generate_series(1,4) x; gave 1,3,6,10 (nodeWindowAgg.c). 3) LATERAL: SELECT g, l.v FROM generate_series(1,2) g, LATERAL (SELECT g*10 AS v) l; gave 10 and 20 (planner and executor). 4) MERGE: MERGE INTO kv t USING (VALUES (1,'c'),(2,'d')) s(k,v) ON t.k=s.k WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET v=s.v WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (k,v) VALUES (s.k,s.v); MERGE 2 on 16.6 (parser/parse_merge.c, executor/nodeModifyTable.c). 5) Upsert: INSERT INTO kv VALUES (1,'b') ON CONFLICT (k) DO UPDATE SET v=excluded.v RETURNING *; (nodeModifyTable.c). 6) Job queues: SELECT * FROM kv ORDER BY k FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1; skips rows other sessions hold (nodeLockRows.c).

1) Function: CREATE FUNCTION dbl(i int) RETURNS int LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN i*2; END $$; dbl(21) gave 42 (commands/functioncmds.c). 2) Procedure: CREATE PROCEDURE bump() ... ; CALL bump(); procedures can run transaction control, functions cannot. 3) Trigger: CREATE TRIGGER kv_ai AFTER INSERT ON kv FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION trg(); my insert wrote 'INSERT 9' to an audit table (commands/trigger.c). 4) Event trigger: CREATE EVENT TRIGGER et ON ddl_command_end EXECUTE FUNCTION ddl_log(); printed 'ddl: CREATE TABLE' (commands/event_trigger.c). 5) Languages: only c, internal, plpgsql, sql exist by default (I listed pg_language). plperl, plpython and pltcl are separate extensions in src/pl/plperl, src/pl/plpython, src/pl/tcl. plpgsql itself is src/pl/plpgsql/src (pl_gram.y, pl_comp.c, pl_exec.c).

1) Full-text: SELECT to_tsvector('english','The quick brown foxes jumped') @@ to_tsquery('english','fox & jump'); true, because stemming turns foxes into fox (src/backend/tsearch: wparser_def.c, dict_*.c, ts_parse.c; ranking in utils/adt/tsrank.c). 2) GIN on text search: CREATE INDEX ON w USING gin (to_tsvector('english', t)); (src/backend/access/gin). 3) Trigrams: CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm; SELECT t, similarity(t,'postgrs') FROM w ORDER BY 2 DESC; gave postgre 0.6 then postgres 0.545 (contrib/pg_trgm/trgm_op.c). 4) Fuzzy index: CREATE INDEX ON w USING gin (t gin_trgm_ops); speeds LIKE and similarity (trgm_gin.c, trgm_gist.c). 5) jsonb search: a GIN index on a jsonb column speeds the @> operator (utils/adt/jsonb_gin.c). 6) Dictionaries and parsers are pluggable: see src/backend/tsearch/dicts and dict_ispell.c.

1) Transactional DDL: BEGIN; CREATE TABLE td(i int); ROLLBACK; then to_regclass('td') is NULL (access/transam/xact.c). 2) CHECK constraint: price numeric CHECK (price>0); inserting -1 gave 'violates check constraint "c_price_check"' (catalog/heap.c). 3) Generated column: b int GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a*2) STORED; a=3 gave b=6 (virtual columns are 18+). 4) Row level security: ALTER TABLE doc ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; CREATE POLICY p ON doc USING (owner = current_user); as role alice only alice's row showed (commands/policy.c, rewrite/rowsecurity.c). 5) Other constraints: PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, FOREIGN KEY, EXCLUDE (commands/tablecmds.c, utils/adt/ri_triggers.c for foreign key checks).

1) LISTEN/NOTIFY: LISTEN ch; NOTIFY ch, 'hi'; psql printed 'Asynchronous notification "ch" with payload "hi"' (commands/async.c: Async_Listen, Async_Notify, AtCommit_Notify). 2) COPY: COPY (SELECT 1 AS a, 'x' AS b) TO STDOUT WITH CSV HEADER; (commands/copy.c DoCopy, copyfrom.c, copyto.c). 3) Foreign data wrappers: CREATE EXTENSION postgres_fdw; CREATE SERVER ... ; CREATE FOREIGN TABLE kv_remote(...) SERVER loop; SELECT count(*) FROM kv_remote; returned 4 (src/backend/foreign/foreign.c, commands/foreigncmds.c, contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c). 4) Publications: CREATE PUBLICATION pub FOR TABLE kv; (commands/publicationcmds.c). 5) Logical decoding: needs wal_level=logical; SELECT pg_create_logical_replication_slot('s','pgoutput'); then pg_logical_slot_peek_binary_changes returned changes after an INSERT (replication/logical/decode.c, reorderbuffer.c, replication/pgoutput/pgoutput.c; contrib/test_decoding is a readable example plugin).

1) CREATE EXTENSION reads a .control file and a SQL script (commands/extension.c). 2) pg_stat_statements: add it to shared_preload_libraries, CREATE EXTENSION, SELECT calls FROM pg_stat_statements; (contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c). 3) pgcrypto: crypt('pw', gen_salt('bf')) and digest('a','sha256') (contrib/pgcrypto/pgcrypto.c, crypt-blowfish.c). 4) hstore and citext: 'a=>1,b=>2'::hstore -> 'b' gave 2, and 'ABC'::citext = 'abc' is true (contrib/hstore/hstore_op.c, contrib/citext/citext.c). 5) uuid-ossp: uuid_generate_v4() (contrib/uuid-ossp/uuid-ossp.c). 6) Inspection tools: pageinspect page_header(get_raw_page('kv',0)) gave lower 56, upper 7872; amcheck bt_index_check('kv_pkey') returned cleanly (contrib/pageinspect/rawpage.c, contrib/amcheck/verify_nbtree.c). postgres_fdw and pg_trgm are covered above.

diagram.claim: A SQL statement goes through parser, rewriter, planner and executor, and each built-in feature plugs in at one of these stages or in the catalogs and extension layer.

interview.q: Which PL languages come installed in a fresh database?
answer: plpgsql, plus the sql and internal and c languages.
I listed pg_language on a new database and saw exactly: c, internal, plpgsql, sql.
plperl, plpython and pltcl are built from src/pl only if you configure them, and then loaded with CREATE EXTENSION.
interview.trap: Saying plpython is built in. It is optional and needs a build flag.

interview.q: What is the difference between a function and a procedure?
answer: A function returns a value and is used inside queries.
A procedure is run with CALL and can COMMIT or ROLLBACK inside its body.
Both are stored in pg_proc; prokind tells them apart.

interview.q: Where does the code for jsonb live, and what indexes help it?
answer: src/backend/utils/adt/jsonb*.c.
A GIN index (jsonb_gin.c) speeds containment @> and key-exists ? operators.
jsonb is stored in a parsed binary form, so it does not keep key order or duplicate keys.
interview.trap: Confusing json (stores the text as typed) with jsonb (binary, deduplicated).

interview.q: How do INSERT ... ON CONFLICT and MERGE differ?
answer: ON CONFLICT relies on a unique index and is atomic under concurrency.
MERGE joins a source to a target and can do update, delete or insert per row. It can raise a unique violation under races.
Both are executed in nodeModifyTable.c.
MERGE ... RETURNING and merge_action() arrived in 17; on 16.6 I got a syntax error.
interview.trap: Assuming MERGE is a drop-in upsert with the same concurrency guarantees.

interview.q: How does SKIP LOCKED work for queues?
answer: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED ignores rows another transaction has locked.
Workers can each grab different jobs without waiting.
The handling is in executor/nodeLockRows.c (the 'couldn't lock tuple in SKIP LOCKED mode' branch).
Yes. BEGIN; CREATE TABLE ...; ROLLBACK leaves no table. I checked: to_regclass returned NULL.
Catalog rows are ordinary heap tuples, so an aborted transaction leaves no visible catalog change. Cache invalidation then tells other backends.
A few commands cannot run in a transaction block, for example CREATE DATABASE and CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
interview.trap: Thinking all DDL is rollbackable. Some utility commands are not.

interview.q: How does row level security get applied to a query?
answer: Policies are stored in pg_policy.
The rewriter adds policy conditions to the query (rewrite/rowsecurity.c) before planning.
Table owners bypass RLS unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set; superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass it.
interview.trap: Testing as the table owner or superuser and thinking RLS is broken.

interview.q: Why can LISTEN/NOTIFY messages arrive late, and what are its limits?
answer: Notifications are sent only when the sending transaction commits (AtCommit_Notify in async.c).
A listening client sees them between its own commands.
Payload is limited to under 8000 bytes, and there is a shared queue that can fill up (pg_notification_queue_usage()).
interview.trap: Using NOTIFY as a reliable message queue. Messages are lost if nobody is listening.

interview.q: What does logical decoding need to work, and who reads the output?
answer: wal_level must be logical and you need a replication slot.
decode.c reads WAL, reorderbuffer.c groups changes per transaction, and an output plugin (pgoutput, or test_decoding) formats them.
Publications and subscriptions are built on top of this.
interview.trap: Forgetting to drop an unused slot; it holds WAL and can fill the disk.

interview.q: How is an extension installed and what is in it?
answer: A .control file, one or more SQL scripts, and often a shared library.
CREATE EXTENSION runs the script and records the objects so DROP EXTENSION removes them together (commands/extension.c).
pg_stat_statements also needs shared_preload_libraries and a restart.
interview.trap: Running CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements without preloading; the view then errors.

contributor_tips: Pick a feature, then follow its regression test. Tests live in src/test/regress/sql and contrib/<name>/sql; expected output is in the matching expected folder.
Contrib modules are the friendliest first patches: small, self-contained, and each has its own Makefile and meson.build.
Always check which version a behaviour came in. This repo is 20devel, so compare with the release notes in doc/src/sgml/release-*.sgml before claiming a bug.
When you add a new SQL-visible function, you must edit src/include/catalog/pg_proc.dat and bump catversion.
Run make check (or meson test) before sending a patch. Patches go to the pgsql-hackers mailing list, not GitHub pull requests.

glossary.meaning: Abstract data type. The folder src/backend/utils/adt holds built-in types and their functions.
Optional extension modules shipped in the Postgres source tree.
Common table expression, the WITH clause.
Foreign data wrapper. A plugin that lets you query outside data as a table.
Generalized inverted index. Good for arrays, jsonb and text search.
Row level security. Policies hide rows per user.
Write-ahead log. Every change is written here first.
Turning WAL into row-level changes that other systems can read.
Procedural language, a language you can write server functions in.
Insert, or update if the row already exists (ON CONFLICT).

file_tree.what: Built-in data types and their functions (jsonb.c, rangetypes.c, uuid.c, enum.c, arrayfuncs.c, rowtypes.c, tsvector.c)
Full-text search parser, dictionaries, ispell (wparser_def.c, ts_parse.c, dict_*.c, spell.c)
Utility commands: async.c, copy.c, copyfrom.c, copyto.c, event_trigger.c, extension.c, trigger.c, policy.c, publicationcmds.c, foreigncmds.c
Plan execution nodes (nodeModifyTable.c, nodeLockRows.c, nodeWindowAgg.c, nodeRecursiveunion.c, nodeCtescan.c, nodeForeignscan.c)
Rule rewriting and row level security (rowsecurity.c)
The built-in logical replication output plugin (pgoutput.c)
Optional modules: pg_stat_statements, pgcrypto, postgres_fdw, pg_trgm, amcheck, pageinspect, hstore, citext, uuid-ossp and more

verified_by_running: Ran a scratch PostgreSQL 16.6 (Homebrew) in a temp dir on port 54329 with a unix socket only; stopped it and deleted the data dir.
Array contains, jsonb path, daterange intersection, enum compare, composite field, gen_random_uuid all returned expected values.
tsvector @@ tsquery with stemming returned true; recursive CTE sum returned 15; window running sum gave 1,3,6,10; LATERAL returned 10 and 20.
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING worked; MERGE worked (MERGE 2) but MERGE ... RETURNING gave a syntax error on 16.6 (17+ feature).
SKIP LOCKED, plpgsql function and procedure, row trigger and event trigger (NOTICE ddl: CREATE TABLE) all worked.
pg_language on a fresh DB listed only c, internal, plpgsql, sql.
Transactional DDL rollback left no table; CHECK violation error text seen; stored generated column gave 6; RLS as role alice showed only alice's row.
LISTEN/NOTIFY delivered the payload in psql; COPY TO STDOUT CSV HEADER worked; publication and pgoutput logical slot returned changes with wal_level=logical.
postgres_fdw loopback foreign table counted 4 rows; pgcrypto, hstore, citext, uuid-ossp, pageinspect, amcheck, pg_stat_statements all loaded and returned results; pg_available_extensions had 58 rows.

Verified with ls that all cited source paths exist in the 20devel repo (configure says PACKAGE_VERSION 20devel) and grep confirmed merge_action in primnodes.h, generate_uuidv7 in uuid.c, ATTRIBUTE_GENERATED_VIRTUAL in pg_attribute.h.
more: COPY and LISTEN/NOTIFY are utility commands. They skip the planner and go through tcop/utility.c ProcessUtility.
Primary key, unique and exclusion constraints are enforced by index code, not by triggers.
PostGIS, pgvector and TimescaleDB are third-party. They are not in this source tree.
Not covered here but built in: views, materialized views, sequences and identity columns, jsonpath, parallel query, JIT, plan caching, tablespaces and domains.
